judged_text: The recurring-cancel branch still uses references.find - the first calendar reference only - for each remaining booking, even though the surrounding handler was upgraded in this same function to iterate all calendar references. Cancelling a recurring multi-host COLLECTIVE booking - a data shape this PR is the first to create, since each host's calendar event now gets its own reference row - deletes only the first calendar event of each remaining booking, leaving every other host's calendar event live with attendee invites after the entire series is cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the recurring-cancel path still does `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"));` inside the loop over `updatedBookings` (within the `bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings` branch). Since this PR changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and elsewhere upgrades reference handling to `filter(...)`/iterate all `_calendar` references, using `find(...)` here will only delete the first calendar reference per remaining booking, leaving additional host calendar events undeleted in multi-host/collective scenarios.
